title: Glendale Residents Warned of Scam Emails Targeting City Permit Applicants - NewsBreak
text:
31 minutes ago The City of Glendale, California, has issued a warning about scam emails targeting people who have applied for development-related permits. These emails are not from the City. They often include fake invoices and may ask recipients to make wire transfers or click on links to sign documents. The City states that these messages are part of a larger phishing scam in the area.
Officials advise the public not to respond to unexpected emails that request payment, banking details, or urgent action related to City permits. The City says the only approved ways to pay for a permit are through the official portal at GlendaleCA.gov/Permits or by mailing a check as described in official documents.
To confirm if an invoice is real, recipients should check if the sender’s email ends with “@GlendaleCA.gov,” log in to their permit portal, or call (818) 548-3200. The City also recommends not clicking on links or opening attachments in suspicious emails.
Glendale officials are monitoring the situation and ask anyone who receives suspicious messages about permits or payments to contact the City. People who think they have been scammed or want to report suspicious activity should call the Glendale Police Department at (818) 548-4840.
Glendale is the fourth largest city in Los Angeles County, with a population of about 200,000. The City says it is working to protect residents and keep official transactions secure.
